V p374.text: From the artistic point of view, the comic is an imitation; the grotesque, a creation. The comic is an imitation mixed with a certain degree of creative capacity, or, in other words, of artistic ideality.

V p375.text: From now on I shall refer to the grotesque as the absolute comic, in contrast to the ordinary comic, which I shall call the significative comic. The significative comic speaks a language that is clearer, easier for the common man to understand, and especially easier to analyse, its element being obviously double: art and the moral idea; but the absolute comic, coming as it does much closer to nature, appears as a unity that must be grasped intuitively.
